summary: In the United States, Teriflunomide carries a boxed warning—the strongest warning from the FDA—due to the risk of harm to an unborn baby and severe liver damage, including acute liver failure that may require a transplant [3][6]. The FDA label also warns that the medicine can lower white blood cells, which are cells that help fight infections [6]. Based on a small computer model rather than tests on people, the drug received a medium score of 50 for liver risk and a low score of 30 for heart risk [M]. Additionally, a clinical trial involving a procedure to quickly remove the drug was stopped early after it was determined that the risks outweighed the benefits [9].
